slot.brief: Identify Lucas reagent and how it distinguishes 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols by turbidity appearance time.

stem: At room temperature, which option gives the Lucas reagent and turbidity appearance for $1^\circ$, $2^\circ$ and $3^\circ$ alcohols, in that order?
options: Concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$; immediate, after a few minutes, only on heating
Concentrated $\text{HCl}$ alone; only on heating, after a few minutes, immediate
Dilute $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$; only on heating, after a few minutes, immediate
Concentrated $\text{HCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$; only on heating, after a few minutes, immediate

verdicts.working: Lucas reagent is concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂. At room temperature, primary alcohols react very slowly (turbidity only on heating), secondary alcohols turn turbid after a few minutes, and tertiary alcohols turn turbid immediately.

working:
Lucas reagent: concentrated $\text{HCl}$ + anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$.
At room temperature: $3^\circ$ alcohol, immediate turbidity; $2^\circ$, after a few minutes; $1^\circ$, no turbidity (reacts only on heating).

Independent check: Lucas reagent is concentrated HCl with anhydrous ZnCl₂. At room temperature, primary alcohols react very slowly (turbidity only on heating), secondary alcohols turn turbid after a few minutes, and tertiary alcohols turn turbid immediately.
solution: Lucas reagent is concentrated $\text{HCl}$ with anhydrous $\text{ZnCl}_2$. At room temperature, $1^\circ$ alcohols turn turbid only on heating, $2^\circ$ alcohols after a few minutes, and $3^\circ$ alcohols immediately.
